clinical_observations.content: Sabrina participated in an in-clinic evaluation with her mother present. She exhibited a cheerful and cooperative affect initially, though her level of distractibility became apparent as the session progressed, impacting her attention span. Sabrina's muscle tone appeared within normal limits, with appropriate range of motion in upper and lower extremities. During structured tasks, she required maximal verbal and minimal visual cues to sustain participation, displaying variable engagement patterns. Self-directed activities elicited higher levels of interest, although her fine motor coordination struggled to meet task demands, necessitating hand-over-hand assistance. Testing validity was impacted by these factors, prompting specific modifications such as frequent redirection and simplified task instructions. Observations indicate potential concerns in visual-motor integration, with her performance reflecting inconsistencies likely due to increased distractibility.
